doc_friction.issue: Step 0 says fix each open entry first, but all 12 open entries are control-plane fixes already sitting in their own open PRs awaiting owner approval; the list (redteam.py open) does not show the PR, so each run re-checks open PRs by hand to learn there is nothing to do. Suggest redteam.py open print the patched_in/pending PR when one exists.
Length limits (seo_title <= 70, description <= 160) are not in CLAUDE.md or goals.md 'Write about the work'; found only by running the check after the first push.

deviations.why: Step 0 asks to fix open entries before seeding; every entry is control plane with an open PR already (fix written, waiting on owner approval).
deviations.did: Checked each against the open PR list, left them untouched, went to seeding.
deviations.result: No duplicate control-plane PRs; run time went to the new ZATCA check, where 4 real defects were found.

mutants.note: Attribute local name of a prefixed attribute; only changes order when two prefixes share one namespace URI. Added a C14N test with p and q both bound to urn:p.

Equivalent under V8 (Node, Chromium) only: the mutant returns 0 where 1 is due, and V8's Array.prototype.sort branches on < 0 alone; 200 shuffles each of 4, 10, 33, 70 and 200 declarations all sorted correctly with the mutant comparator. An engine whose merge takes the left element on <= 0 could misorder, and no suite here runs one. Added a reverse-order declaration test anyway (it guards removing the sort).

real_defects.issue: A DigestValue that is not base64 (e.g. base64url '-'/'_') made checkZatcaStamp throw 'not base64' at the signature check; report.mjs's outer try turned the whole file into a read error, so every finding for that file was lost. Fix: verification failure (KSA-STAMP-03) beside KSA-STAMP-01.
decodeQrTlv read a long-form length (0x81/0x82) cut off at the end of the QR as NaN and returned an empty field instead of throwing, so a truncated QR passed as readable rather than KSA-STAMP-04.

checkZatcaChain took Number('') = 0 as a counter, so a batch with one invoice lacking an ICV and a device's first invoice (ICV 1, first-invoice PIH) failed the latter with a false KSA-STAMP-20 error. Fix: counters must be plain decimal integers.

Found by the new fuzz test: a ds:X509Certificate that is not base64 threw 'not base64' at the xades:CertDigest comparison (fromBase64(certText) outside any try), so the batch report listed the file as unreadable instead of KSA-STAMP-17/18.
